text: 烟笼寒水月笼沙，夜泊秦淮近酒家
pinyin: yān lǒng hán shuǐ yuè lǒng shā, yè bó qín huái jìn jiǔ jiā
literal: mist · shroud · cold · water, moon · shroud · sand, night · moor · Qinhuai · near · wine-shop
natural: mist veils the cold water and moonlight veils the sand; at night I moor by the Qinhuai, close to the taverns

meaning.en: Du Mu's opening couplet: a misty, moonlit night on the Qinhuai River, where he moors beside the wine-houses.
meaning.zh: 杜牧《泊秦淮》开篇两句：烟雾月色笼罩着秦淮河，诗人夜晚把船停在酒家近旁。

equivalents: a misty moonlit night by the river
mist and moon over cold water

examples.zh: “烟笼寒水月笼沙，夜泊秦淮近酒家”，几笔就勾出了秦淮夜色。
examples.en: 'Mist veils the cold water, moon veils the sand; at night I moor by the Qinhuai near the taverns' sketches the Qinhuai night in a few strokes.

examples.zh: 游船驶过夫子庙，导游轻声念起烟笼寒水月笼沙，夜泊秦淮近酒家。
examples.en: As the boat passed the Confucius Temple, the guide softly recited 'mist veils the cold water, moon veils the sand; at night I moor by the Qinhuai near the taverns'.

story.en: Du Mu (803-852?), a late-Tang poet, wrote this quatrain while mooring on the Qinhuai River in Jinling (Nanjing).
story.zh: 晚唐诗人杜牧（803—852?）夜泊金陵秦淮河时作此七绝。

usage.en: Quoted when describing the Qinhuai River by night, or a hazy, moonlit riverside scene. The poem goes on to a quiet rebuke of the revelry of the time (商女不知亡国恨，隔江犹唱后庭花).
usage.zh: 描写秦淮夜景或朦胧月夜的水边景色时常被引用。全诗后两句借“商女”暗讽当时的醉生梦死（商女不知亡国恨，隔江犹唱后庭花）。

text: 春心莫共花争发，一寸相思一寸灰
pinyin: chūn xīn mò gòng huā zhēng fā, yī cùn xiāng sī yī cùn huī
literal: spring · heart · do not · with · flowers · vie · to bloom, one · inch · longing · one · inch · ash
natural: do not let your heart of spring vie with the flowers to bloom; every inch of longing turns to an inch of ash

meaning.en: Li Shangyin on hopeless love: do not let the heart stir with the spring blossoms, for each inch of longing only burns down to ash.
meaning.zh: 李商隐写无望的相思：不要让春心与百花一同萌发，每一寸相思都化作一寸死灰。

equivalents: every inch of longing turns to ash
love that burns itself out

examples.zh: 失恋之后，她在日记里抄下“春心莫共花争发，一寸相思一寸灰”。
examples.en: After the break-up she copied 'do not let your spring heart vie with the flowers; every inch of longing is an inch of ash' into her diary.

examples.zh: 老师讲李商隐的爱情诗时，特别提到了春心莫共花争发，一寸相思一寸灰这一联。
examples.en: Introducing Li Shangyin's love poetry, the teacher singled out the couplet '春心莫共花争发，一寸相思一寸灰'.

origin.source: 李商隐《无题》（飒飒东风细雨来）

story.en: Li Shangyin (c. 813-858) wrote this untitled poem, which opens '飒飒东风细雨来'; the couplet is its closing lines.
story.zh: 李商隐（约813—858）《无题》以“飒飒东风细雨来”开篇，此联为其结尾。

usage.en: Quoted for love that is doomed or unspoken. 春心 means the stirring of love; 灰 (ash) echoes the candle-and-ash imagery of Li Shangyin's love poems.
usage.zh: 多用来写无望或难以言说的爱情。“春心”指萌动的爱意，“灰”与李商隐诗中常见的蜡烛成灰之意象相呼应。

text: 庄生晓梦迷蝴蝶，望帝春心托杜鹃
pinyin: zhuāng shēng xiǎo mèng mí hú dié, wàng dì chūn xīn tuō dù juān
literal: Zhuang · master · dawn · dream · bewildered by · butterfly, Wangdi · spring · heart · entrust · cuckoo
natural: Master Zhuang's dawn dream was lost in a butterfly; Emperor Wang's springtime heart lodged in a cuckoo

meaning.en: Two allusions in Li Shangyin's 《锦瑟》: Zhuangzi dreaming he was a butterfly, and the legendary king Wangdi whose grief became the cuckoo's cry; a meditation on the blur between dream and reality.
meaning.zh: 李商隐《锦瑟》中的两个典故：庄周梦蝶，与望帝化为杜鹃啼血；写梦与现实的难以分辨。

equivalents: is it a dream or is it real
dream and reality blurred

examples.zh: 读到“庄生晓梦迷蝴蝶，望帝春心托杜鹃”，不少同学都被诗里的典故难住了。
examples.en: Many students were stumped by the allusions in 'Zhuang's dawn dream bewildered by a butterfly; Wangdi's spring heart entrusted to a cuckoo'.

examples.zh: 这篇散文以庄生晓梦迷蝴蝶，望帝春心托杜鹃作题记。
examples.en: The essay takes 'Zhuang Sheng's dawn dream was lost in a butterfly; Wangdi's spring heart lodged in a cuckoo' as its epigraph.

story.en: In 《锦瑟》 Li Shangyin draws on the Zhuangzi butterfly dream and on the legend of King Wangdi of Shu, whose spirit was said to turn into a cuckoo.
story.zh: 李商隐《锦瑟》用了《庄子》庄周梦蝶的典故，以及蜀王望帝魂化杜鹃的传说。

usage.en: Quoted for the dream-or-reality theme or the pain of a heart left with only memory. 《锦瑟》 is among the most debated of Chinese poems; its meaning has never been settled.
usage.zh: 常用于梦与现实、情思寄托之类的主题。《锦瑟》是中国诗史上争议最多的作品之一，诗意至今没有定论。

text: 沧海月明珠有泪，蓝田日暖玉生烟
pinyin: cāng hǎi yuè míng zhū yǒu lèi, lán tián rì nuǎn yù shēng yān
literal: blue · sea · moon · bright · pearls · have · tears, Lantian · sun · warm · jade · give off · mist
natural: under the bright moon on the blue sea the pearls weep; in the warm sun at Lantian the jade breathes mist

meaning.en: A famous, much-interpreted couplet from Li Shangyin's 《锦瑟》: beauty seen but untouchable, tears turned to pearls, jade whose haze vanishes when approached.
meaning.zh: 李商隐《锦瑟》中最著名、也最难解的一联：美好之物可望而不可即，泪化为珠，玉烟遥看可见、近观则无。

equivalents: beauty that can be seen but not touched
a haze of regret

examples.zh: “沧海月明珠有泪，蓝田日暖玉生烟”，意境极美，却很难说清到底写的是什么。
examples.en: 'Under the bright moon on the blue sea the pearls weep; in warm Lantian the jade breathes mist' is beautiful, yet hard to pin down.

examples.zh: 她把沧海月明珠有泪，蓝田日暖玉生烟抄在书签上。
examples.en: She copied 'the pearls weep under the moon on the blue sea; the jade breathes mist in warm Lantian' onto a bookmark.

story.en: The couplet draws on the legend of mermaids whose tears become pearls, and on the jade of Lantian Mountain, from which mist is said to rise.
story.zh: 此联用了鲛人泣泪成珠的传说，以及蓝田山美玉生烟的说法。

usage.en: Quoted for a dreamlike, wistful beauty. 蓝田 is a mountain famed for jade. Readers have long read the couplet in different ways (grief, love, a poet's own career), so no single interpretation is standard.
usage.zh: 用来形容迷离伤感的美。蓝田是出产美玉的名山。此联历来解说不一（悼亡、爱情、身世之感等），没有定说。

text: 忽见陌头杨柳色，悔教夫婿觅封侯
pinyin: hū jiàn mò tóu yáng liǔ sè, huǐ jiào fū xù mì fēng hóu
literal: suddenly · see · lane · head · willow · colour, regret · let · husband · seek · title of marquis
natural: suddenly she sees the willows green at the roadside and regrets sending her husband off to seek a title

meaning.en: From Wang Changling's 《闺怨》: a young wife, seeing the spring willows, regrets having urged her husband to seek rank and glory far away.
meaning.zh: 王昌龄《闺怨》：少妇忽然看见路边柳色，后悔当初让丈夫远行去博取功名。

equivalents: regret for sending a husband off to seek fame
a wife's regret at ambition's cost

examples.zh: “忽见陌头杨柳色，悔教夫婿觅封侯”写出了戍边将士妻子的怨情。
examples.en: 'Suddenly she sees the willows green by the road, regretting that she sent her husband to win a title' captures the sorrow of a soldier's wife.

examples.zh: 在机场送别丈夫出国进修，她心里忽然冒出忽见陌头杨柳色，悔教夫婿觅封侯这句诗。
examples.en: Seeing her husband off at the airport to study abroad, the line 'suddenly she sees the willows green by the road and regrets sending him to seek a title' came to her mind.

story.en: Wang Changling (c. 698-756), a High Tang master of the quatrain, wrote 《闺怨》 ('A Young Wife's Lament') in four lines.
story.zh: 盛唐七绝名家王昌龄（约698—756）作《闺怨》，全诗四句。

usage.en: Quoted, sometimes jokingly, for the regret of one left at home while a partner chases a career. Willows are a traditional symbol of parting (折柳送别).
usage.zh: 常用来表达（有时是半开玩笑地）为追求事业而远行的亲人留下的惆怅。柳在传统中象征离别（折柳送别）。

text: 青海长云暗雪山，孤城遥望玉门关
pinyin: qīng hǎi cháng yún àn xuě shān, gū chéng yáo wàng yù mén guān
literal: Qinghai · long · clouds · darken · snow · mountains, lone · fort · far · gaze · Jade Gate Pass
natural: long clouds over Qinghai darken the snowy mountains; from the lone fort I gaze far towards Jade Gate Pass

meaning.en: Opening lines of Wang Changling's frontier poem: a vast, bleak border landscape seen from a lonely garrison town.
meaning.zh: 王昌龄边塞诗的起笔：从孤零零的戍城望去，青海上空长云遮暗雪山，边塞苍茫。

equivalents: a lone fort under darkened snowy peaks
the loneliness of the frontier

examples.zh: “青海长云暗雪山，孤城遥望玉门关”几笔就写出了西北边塞的辽阔与荒凉。
examples.en: 'Long clouds over Qinghai darken the snowy mountains; from the lone fort I gaze towards Jade Gate Pass' conveys the vastness and bleakness of the north-west frontier in a few strokes.

examples.zh: 站在嘉峪关城楼上，导游念起青海长云暗雪山，孤城遥望玉门关。
examples.en: On the tower at Jiayuguan, the guide recited 'long clouds over Qinghai darken the snowy mountains; from the lone fort I gaze towards Jade Gate Pass'.

origin.source: 王昌龄《从军行七首》其四

story.en: Wang Changling wrote seven frontier songs under the title 《从军行》; this couplet opens the fourth.
story.zh: 王昌龄作《从军行》七首，此联为其四的开头。

usage.en: Quoted for frontier scenery and the soldier's far-off longing for home. The poem continues '黄沙百战穿金甲，不破楼兰终不还'.
usage.zh: 常用来描写边塞风光和戍边将士的思乡之情。下两句为“黄沙百战穿金甲，不破楼兰终不还”。

text: 北风卷地白草折，胡天八月即飞雪
pinyin: běi fēng juǎn dì bái cǎo zhé, hú tiān bā yuè jí fēi xuě
literal: north · wind · sweep · ground · white · grass · snaps, barbarian · sky · eighth · month · already · flies · snow
natural: the north wind sweeps the ground and snaps the white grass; in the frontier sky it already snows in the eighth month

meaning.en: Cen Shen's opening to his snow song: a ferocious northern wind and snow already falling in early autumn on the frontier.
meaning.zh: 岑参《白雪歌送武判官归京》的开篇：北风席卷大地，白草折断，边塞八月就已飞雪。

equivalents: snow in early autumn on the frontier
a bitter northern gale

examples.zh: “北风卷地白草折，胡天八月即飞雪”，寥寥十四字就让人感到边塞的苦寒。
examples.en: 'The north wind sweeps the ground and snaps the white grass; in the frontier sky it snows already in the eighth month' makes the bitter cold of the frontier felt in fourteen characters.

examples.zh: 新疆的初雪来得早，当地人常说北风卷地白草折，胡天八月即飞雪。
examples.en: First snow comes early in Xinjiang, and locals often say 'the north wind sweeps the ground and snaps the white grass; in the frontier sky it snows in the eighth month'.

origin.source: 岑参《白雪歌送武判官归京》

story.en: Cen Shen (c. 715-770), the best-known frontier poet of the Tang, wrote this song while serving in the north-west, seeing off Wu, a colleague returning to the capital.
story.zh: 唐代最著名的边塞诗人岑参（约715—770）在西北军幕时作此诗，送同僚武判官回京。

usage.en: Quoted to describe a sudden early cold snap or harsh northern weather. 胡天 = the sky of the western regions; 八月 is the eighth lunar month, i.e. early autumn.
usage.zh: 形容骤然降温或北方严寒时常被引用。“胡天”指西域的天空；八月为农历八月，即初秋。

text: 千里黄云白日曛，北风吹雁雪纷纷
pinyin: qiān lǐ huáng yún bái rì xūn, běi fēng chuī yàn xuě fēn fēn
literal: thousand · li · yellow · clouds · white · sun · dim, north · wind · blow · geese · snow · thick and fast
natural: yellow clouds stretch a thousand li and dim the white sun; the north wind drives the geese and the snow falls thick

meaning.en: Opening of Gao Shi's farewell to Dong Da: a leaden sky, a north wind and snow set the scene for parting.
meaning.zh: 高适《别董大》的开头：千里黄云遮暗日光，北风吹着雁群，大雪纷飞，为送别渲染气氛。

equivalents: a bleak sky for a farewell
yellow clouds and driving snow

examples.zh: “千里黄云白日曛，北风吹雁雪纷纷”，接着就是那句有名的“莫愁前路无知己”。
examples.en: 'Yellow clouds for a thousand li dim the white sun; the north wind drives the geese through the thick snow' leads to the famous 'fear not that you will have no friend ahead'.

examples.zh: 送别那天下起大雪，他忽然想起千里黄云白日曛，北风吹雁雪纷纷。
examples.en: On the day of the farewell it snowed heavily, and he suddenly recalled 'yellow clouds for a thousand li dim the white sun; the north wind drives the geese through the thick snow'.

story.en: Gao Shi (c. 704-765) wrote this poem for the lutenist Dong Tinglan (Dong Da), probably around 746.
story.zh: 高适（约704—765）为琴师董庭兰（董大）送行而作，约在天宝五载（746）前后。

usage.en: Quoted for wintry farewells; usually followed by '莫愁前路无知己，天下谁人不识君'. 曛 means dim, dusky.
usage.zh: 多用于冬日送别；后接“莫愁前路无知己，天下谁人不识君”。“曛”意为昏暗。

text: 儿童相见不相识，笑问客从何处来
pinyin: ér tóng xiāng jiàn bù xiāng shí, xiào wèn kè cóng hé chù lái
literal: children · meet · not · recognise, smiling · ask · guest · from · what · place · come
natural: the children see me but do not know me, and ask with a smile where the visitor has come from

meaning.en: The closing lines of He Zhizhang's 'Returning Home': after decades away, the old man is taken for a stranger in his own village.
meaning.zh: 贺知章《回乡偶书》的结尾：离家数十年的老人回到故乡，反被村里的孩子当作外来客。

equivalents: a stranger in his own hometown
returning after decades away

examples.zh: 离乡三十年，回到村口时孩子们笑问他“客从何处来”，真应了儿童相见不相识，笑问客从何处来。
examples.en: After thirty years away, the children asked him with a smile where the visitor was from, just as in 'the children see me but do not know me and ask where the visitor comes from'.

examples.zh: 在语文课上，同学们背诵了儿童相见不相识，笑问客从何处来。
examples.en: In Chinese class the pupils recited 'the children see me but do not know me, and ask with a smile where the visitor has come from'.

origin.source: 贺知章《回乡偶书二首》其二

story.en: He Zhizhang (659-744) left his native Yue (Zhejiang) as a young man and returned in old age; the poem is traditionally said to date from that return.
story.zh: 贺知章（659—744）年少离开家乡越州，晚年回乡，此诗相传作于此时。

usage.en: Quoted for homecoming after a long absence, with a note of gentle sadness. It is one of the first poems Chinese children learn. The preceding line is 乡音无改鬓毛衰.
usage.zh: 多用来写久别归乡、物是人非，带着淡淡的伤感。这是中国儿童最早学的古诗之一。前一句为“乡音无改鬓毛衰”。

text: 碧玉妆成一树高，万条垂下绿丝绦
pinyin: bì yù zhuāng chéng yī shù gāo, wàn tiáo chuí xià lǜ sī tāo
literal: jade · dressed · complete · one · tree · tall, ten thousand · branches · hang · down · green · silk · cords
natural: a tree tall as if dressed in green jade, with ten thousand branches hanging down like green silk ribbons

meaning.en: The opening of He Zhizhang's 'Ode to the Willow': the willow in spring, pictured as a lady dressed in jade with silk ribbons.
meaning.zh: 贺知章《咏柳》开头：把春天的柳树比作一身碧玉装扮的女子，万条柳枝如绿色丝带垂下。

equivalents: a willow like a lady in green
willow branches like silk ribbons

examples.zh: “碧玉妆成一树高，万条垂下绿丝绦”，一句话就写出了柳树的婀娜。
examples.en: 'A tree tall as if dressed in green jade, ten thousand branches hanging like green silk ribbons' captures the grace of the willow in one line.

examples.zh: 春天到了，小学生在校园的柳树下读起碧玉妆成一树高，万条垂下绿丝绦。
examples.en: With spring here, primary pupils under the willows in the schoolyard read aloud 'a tree tall as if dressed in green jade, ten thousand branches hanging like green silk ribbons'.

story.en: He Zhizhang (659-744), a Tang court official and poet, wrote this four-line poem on the willow; it is one of the best-known in the Chinese primary curriculum.
story.zh: 唐代官员兼诗人贺知章（659—744）作此四句咏柳诗，是小学语文教材中最有名的篇目之一。

usage.en: A first couplet that children learn; quoted for willows in spring. The poem ends '不知细叶谁裁出，二月春风似剪刀'.
usage.zh: 儿童启蒙诗句，常用来描写春天的柳树。全诗结尾为“不知细叶谁裁出，二月春风似剪刀”。

text: 白毛浮绿水，红掌拨清波
pinyin: bái máo fú lǜ shuǐ, hóng zhǎng bō qīng bō
literal: white · feathers · float · on · green · water, red · feet · paddle · clear · waves
natural: white feathers float on the green water, red webbed feet paddle the clear waves

meaning.en: Two vivid lines from Luo Binwang's 'Ode to the Goose', written, according to tradition, when he was a child: colour and motion in a few words.
meaning.zh: 骆宾王《咏鹅》中的名句，相传作于他七岁时：寥寥几字，色彩与动态俱现。

equivalents: white feathers on green water, red feet in clear waves
geese paddling on a pond

examples.zh: 孩子指着池塘里的鹅，脱口念出“白毛浮绿水，红掌拨清波”。
examples.en: The child pointed at the geese in the pond and blurted out 'white feathers float on the green water, red feet paddle the clear waves'.

examples.zh: 《咏鹅》里的白毛浮绿水，红掌拨清波，色彩对比鲜明。
examples.en: In 'Ode to the Goose' the lines 'white feathers float on the green water, red feet paddle the clear waves' make a vivid colour contrast.

story.en: Luo Binwang (c. 619-687), one of the 'Four Talents of the Early Tang', is traditionally said to have composed this poem at the age of seven.
story.zh: 骆宾王（约619—687）为“初唐四杰”之一，相传此诗作于七岁。

usage.en: A children's classic; quoted for geese or for a simple, colourful scene. The poem opens '鹅，鹅，鹅，曲项向天歌'.
usage.zh: 儿童启蒙名句，常用来写鹅或简洁鲜明的画面。全诗开头为“鹅，鹅，鹅，曲项向天歌”。

text: 春江潮水连海平，海上明月共潮生
pinyin: chūn jiāng cháo shuǐ lián hǎi píng, hǎi shàng míng yuè gòng cháo shēng
literal: spring · river · tide · water · joins · sea · level, sea · above · bright · moon · together with · tide · rises
natural: the spring river's tide is level with the sea; above the sea the bright moon rises with the tide

meaning.en: The famous opening of 《春江花月夜》: a vast scene of river, sea, tide and moon.
meaning.zh: 《春江花月夜》的著名开篇：江、海、潮、月连成一片，意境开阔。

equivalents: moon and tide rising together over a spring river
a moonlit river meeting the sea

examples.zh: “春江潮水连海平，海上明月共潮生”被誉为最美的开篇之一。
examples.en: 'The spring river's tide is level with the sea; the bright moon rises with the tide' is praised as one of the most beautiful openings.

examples.zh: 夜里站在入海口看潮，他想起春江潮水连海平，海上明月共潮生。
examples.en: Watching the tide at the river mouth at night, he thought of 'the spring river's tide is level with the sea; the bright moon rises with the tide'.

story.en: Zhang Ruoxu (c. 660-720) is known almost solely for this long poem, which gives a panorama of river, moon and human longing.
story.zh: 张若虚（约660—720）几乎只以这首长诗闻名，诗中展开江月人生的宏阔图景。

date.zh: 唐 · 约7世纪末—8世纪初

usage.en: Quoted for moonlit river or sea scenes. 《春江花月夜》 is a long poem of 36 lines; the scholar Wen Yiduo praised it as the 'poem above poems'.
usage.zh: 常用来描写江海月夜之景。《春江花月夜》全诗三十六句，闻一多誉之为“诗中的诗，顶峰上的顶峰”。

text: 人生代代无穷已，江月年年望相似
pinyin: rén shēng dài dài wú qióng yǐ, jiāng yuè nián nián wàng xiāng sì
literal: human · life · generation · after generation · no · end · stop, river · moon · year · after year · looks · alike
natural: generations of people go on without end, while the moon over the river looks the same year after year

meaning.en: From 《春江花月夜》: human generations pass in an endless chain, yet the moon above the river seems unchanged.
meaning.zh: 《春江花月夜》名句：人类一代代延续不绝，江上之月却年年相似。

equivalents: generations come and go, the moon stays the same
the river moon outlasts us all

examples.zh: 毕业典礼上，校长引用了“人生代代无穷已，江月年年望相似”。
examples.en: At the graduation ceremony the principal quoted 'generations of people go on without end, while the river moon looks the same year after year'.

examples.zh: 看着老家门前不变的月亮，他想到人生代代无穷已，江月年年望相似。
examples.en: Looking at the unchanging moon over his old home, he thought of 'generations go on without end, the river moon looks the same year after year'.

story.en: This couplet comes in the middle of Zhang Ruoxu's poem, where the poet turns from the scenery to reflection on life.
story.zh: 此联位于张若虚全诗中段，诗人由写景转入对人生的思索。

date.zh: 唐 · 约7世纪末—8世纪初

usage.en: Quoted when reflecting on time, generations and the constancy of nature, often with a quiet philosophical note. The next line is '不知江月待何人，但见长江送流水'.
usage.zh: 在感叹时间、代际更替和自然永恒时引用，带有淡淡的哲思。下一句为“不知江月待何人，但见长江送流水”。

text: 最是一年春好处，绝胜烟柳满皇都
pinyin: zuì shì yī nián chūn hǎo chù, jué shèng yān liǔ mǎn huáng dū
literal: most · is · one · year · spring · good · point, far · surpasses · misty · willows · fill · imperial · capital
natural: this is the best of the whole year's spring, far better than the capital full of misty willows

meaning.en: Han Yu on early spring: the first, faint green of the year is lovelier than the full willow-mist of late spring in the capital.
meaning.zh: 韩愈写早春：初春草色若有若无，最是一年春光好处，远胜暮春京城里烟柳满城。

equivalents: early spring is the loveliest
the first hint of green beats full bloom

examples.zh: “最是一年春好处，绝胜烟柳满皇都”，说的是早春才最动人。
examples.en: 'This is the best of the year's spring, far better than the capital full of misty willows' says that early spring is the loveliest.

examples.zh: 三月初公园草色初现，同事笑说这正是最是一年春好处，绝胜烟柳满皇都。
examples.en: In early March the grass was just showing in the park; a colleague joked that this was 'the best of the year's spring, far better than the capital full of misty willows'.

origin.source: 韩愈《早春呈水部张十八员外》

story.en: Han Yu (768-824) sent this poem to his friend Zhang Ji, then an official in the Bureau of Waterways (水部员外郎).
story.zh: 韩愈（768—824）将此诗赠给时任水部员外郎的友人张籍。

usage.en: Quoted for early spring or for the idea that the beginning of something can be lovelier than its full flowering. The preceding couplet is 天街小雨润如酥，草色遥看近却无.
usage.zh: 常用来写早春，或比喻事物初起时的美胜过鼎盛。前一联为“天街小雨润如酥，草色遥看近却无”。

text: 妆罢低声问夫婿，画眉深浅入时无
pinyin: zhuāng bà dī shēng wèn fū xù, huà méi shēn qiǎn rù shí wú
literal: make-up · finished · low · voice · ask · husband, paint · brows · dark · light · in · fashion · or not
natural: her make-up done, she asks her husband in a low voice whether her painted brows are dark or light enough to suit the fashion

meaning.en: Zhu Qingyu's poem, written as a candidate approaching an examiner: a bride's shy question stands for his own anxious 'Will my work please you?'.
meaning.zh: 朱庆馀以新娘自比：新妇梳妆已毕，低声问夫婿眉画得合不合时宜，实际是向主考官探问自己的文章合不合格。

equivalents: will it meet with approval?
asking whether one's work is up to standard

examples.zh: 交稿前他忐忑地问导师，心里想的正是“妆罢低声问夫婿，画眉深浅入时无”。
examples.en: Before handing in his draft he anxiously asked his supervisor, thinking just of 'her make-up done, she asks her husband whether her brows suit the fashion'.

examples.zh: 这首诗表面写新娘，其实“妆罢低声问夫婿，画眉深浅入时无”是借喻考生向主考官请教。
examples.en: On the surface the poem is about a bride, but 'make-up done, she asks her husband in a low voice whether her brows suit the fashion' is really an examinee asking the examiner.

origin.source: 朱庆馀《近试上张籍水部》

story.en: Zhu Qingyu (early 9th c.) sent this poem to the official and poet Zhang Ji shortly before the jinshi examination, to sound out his opinion of his work.
story.zh: 朱庆馀（九世纪初）在进士考试前把此诗呈给张籍，探问对自己文章的看法。

usage.en: Often used for seeking approval of one's work. 入时无 = '合时宜吗?' (无 here is the old question particle, like 否). The poem is a classic example of an extended metaphor.
usage.zh: 常借以表示向人请教、希望作品得到认可。“入时无”即“合时宜吗”（“无”是疑问语气词，同“否”）。此诗是以比喻寄托心意的经典例子。

text: 鸡声茅店月，人迹板桥霜
pinyin: jī shēng máo diàn yuè, rén jì bǎn qiáo shuāng
literal: cock · crow · thatched · inn · moon, human · tracks · plank · bridge · frost
natural: a cock crows, the moon over the thatched inn; footprints on the frost of the plank bridge

meaning.en: A famous couplet made only of images (no verbs): the early-morning start of a traveller leaving a country inn.
meaning.zh: 只用名词意象组成（没有动词）的名联：旅人清晨离开乡间客店时所见的景象。

equivalents: an early start on a frosty morning
dawn at a country inn

examples.zh: “鸡声茅店月，人迹板桥霜”，全句没有一个动词，却让人看到了赶路的清晨。
examples.en: 'A cock crows, the moon over the thatched inn; footprints on the frost of the plank bridge' has not a single verb, yet it shows the traveller's early morning.

examples.zh: 凌晨四点出发进山，山里的景象正是鸡声茅店月，人迹板桥霜。
examples.en: Setting out for the hills at four in the morning, the scene was just 'a cock crows, the moon over the thatched inn; footprints on frost on the plank bridge'.

story.en: Wen Tingyun (c. 812-870) wrote this poem about leaving an inn at dawn on the Shang Mountain road in Shaanxi.
story.zh: 温庭筠（约812—870）作此诗，写清晨离开陕西商山道上客店赶路的情景。

usage.en: Quoted for early-morning journeys and as a model of imagistic writing: a row of bare images in ten characters, admired by Ouyang Xiu.
usage.zh: 常用来写清晨赶路，也是意象并置写法的典范。欧阳修曾对此联十分赞赏。

text: 不知天上宫阙，今夕是何年
pinyin: bù zhī tiān shàng gōng què, jīn xī shì hé nián
literal: not · know · heaven · above · palaces, tonight · is · what · year
natural: I wonder in the palaces of heaven, what year is it tonight

meaning.en: From Su Shi's Mid-Autumn ci: gazing at the moon, the poet wonders what year it is in the heavenly palaces.
meaning.zh: 苏轼中秋词中的名句：对月遥想，不知天上宫阙此夕又是何年。

equivalents: wondering what year it is in heaven
lost in wonder at the moon

examples.zh: 中秋夜抬头望月，他轻声念道“不知天上宫阙，今夕是何年”。
examples.en: Gazing at the moon on Mid-Autumn night, he murmured 'I wonder in the palaces of heaven, what year it is tonight'.

examples.zh: “不知天上宫阙，今夕是何年”这句常被用来说人在节日里的恍惚感。
examples.en: The line 'I wonder in the palaces of heaven what year it is tonight' is often used for the dazed feeling one gets on a festival night.

origin.source: 苏轼《水调歌头·明月几时有》

story.en: Su Shi (1037-1101) wrote this ci at Mizhou on Mid-Autumn of 1076, thinking of his brother Su Zhe.
story.zh: 苏轼（1037—1101）于熙宁九年（1076）中秋在密州作此词，怀念弟弟苏辙。

usage.en: Mid-Autumn favourite, also used for the dreamy sense of losing track of time. The usual text of the preceding line is 明月几时有，把酒问青天.
usage.zh: 中秋常引，也用来表示恍惚、忘了时日的感觉。前一句为“明月几时有，把酒问青天”。

text: 纵使相逢应不识，尘满面，鬓如霜
pinyin: zòng shǐ xiāng féng yīng bù shí, chén mǎn miàn, bìn rú shuāng
literal: even if · meet · surely · not · recognise, dust · fills · face, temples · like · frost
natural: even if we met we would surely not know each other: face full of dust, temples white as frost

meaning.en: From Su Shi's dream-poem for his dead wife: after ten years of grief and hardship he fears she would not recognise him.
meaning.zh: 苏轼悼念亡妻之词：十年生死两茫茫，他想象即使相逢，妻子也认不出风尘满面、鬓发如霜的自己。

equivalents: so aged by grief you would not know me
dust on the face, frost in the hair

examples.zh: “纵使相逢应不识，尘满面，鬓如霜”，把十年的辛酸都写在了脸上。
examples.en: 'Even if we met you would not know me: face full of dust, temples like frost' writes ten years of hardship across the face.

examples.zh: 多年漂泊后回到老家，他想起了纵使相逢应不识，尘满面，鬓如霜。
examples.en: Returning home after years of drifting, he thought of 'even if we met you would not know me: face full of dust, temples like frost'.

origin.source: 苏轼《江城子·乙卯正月二十日夜记梦》

story.en: Su Shi wrote this ci at Mizhou in 1075, ten years after the death of his first wife, Wang Fu.
story.zh: 苏轼于熙宁八年（1075）在密州作此词，时距发妻王弗去世已十年。

usage.en: Quoted for grief, absence and the toll of time. The preceding line is 千里孤坟，无处话凄凉.
usage.zh: 用于表达悼亡之痛、久别和岁月沧桑。前文有“千里孤坟，无处话凄凉”。

text: 老夫聊发少年狂，左牵黄，右擎苍
pinyin: lǎo fū liáo fā shào nián kuáng, zuǒ qiān huáng, yòu qíng cāng
literal: old · man · for once · give vent to · youth's · wildness, left · lead · yellow (hound), right · hold up · grey (hawk)
natural: for once this old fellow gives vent to the wildness of youth: a yellow hound on the left hand, a grey hawk on the right

meaning.en: Opening of Su Shi's hunting ci: though only about forty by Chinese reckoning, he calls himself an old man and sets off with hound and hawk with youthful zest.
meaning.zh: 苏轼出猎词的开头：他当时不过四十岁，却自称“老夫”，左手牵黄犬，右臂托苍鹰，豪情顿生。

equivalents: an old man's youthful dash
a burst of youthful vigour

examples.zh: 退休后他重新骑车远行，笑称自己是“老夫聊发少年狂，左牵黄，右擎苍”。
examples.en: After retiring he took up long-distance cycling again, joking that 'for once this old fellow gives vent to the wildness of youth, a hound on the left, a hawk on the right'.

examples.zh: 爷爷下场踢球，大家都笑他老夫聊发少年狂，左牵黄，右擎苍是没有了，倒是左右开弓地传球。
examples.en: Grandfather joined the match, and everyone laughed that 'the old man was giving vent to the wildness of youth'; no hound and hawk, but passing left and right.

story.en: Su Shi wrote this ci in 1075 while governor of Mizhou (Shandong), after leading a hunting party outside the city.
story.zh: 苏轼于熙宁八年（1075）任密州知州时，出城打猎后作此词。

usage.en: Quoted, usually playfully, when an older person acts with youthful abandon. 黄 = yellow dog, 苍 = grey hawk (the 'old man' was in fact about 39).
usage.zh: 年长者做出年轻人才有的举动时，多半带着玩笑口气引用。“黄”指黄犬，“苍”指苍鹰（苏轼其时实际约三十九岁）。

text: 缺月挂疏桐，漏断人初静
pinyin: quē yuè guà shū tóng, lòu duàn rén chū jìng
literal: waning · moon · hangs · sparse · parasol trees, water-clock · stops · people · just · quiet
natural: a waning moon hangs in the sparse parasol trees; the water-clock has run down and all has just fallen quiet

meaning.en: Su Shi's opening to a lonely night scene: a thin moon in bare trees, the late-night silence.
meaning.zh: 苏轼笔下孤寂夜景的开篇：残月挂在疏落的梧桐上，夜深人静。

equivalents: a thin moon in bare trees at dead of night
the quiet of late night

examples.zh: “缺月挂疏桐，漏断人初静”，短短十个字，便写尽了深夜的孤寂。
examples.en: 'A waning moon hangs in the sparse parasol trees; the water-clock has run down and all has just fallen quiet' sums up late-night solitude in ten characters.

examples.zh: 加班到深夜走出大楼，抬头见缺月挂疏桐，漏断人初静，他一下子安静下来。
examples.en: Leaving the office late at night, he looked up and saw 'a waning moon hanging in the sparse parasol trees; the water-clock run down and all quiet', and fell silent himself.

origin.source: 苏轼《卜算子·黄州定慧院寓居作》

story.en: Su Shi wrote this ci in Huangzhou (c. 1080-1082), where he lived in exile in the Dinghui Monastery.
story.zh: 苏轼贬居黄州（约1080—1082）时，寓居定慧院，作此词。

usage.en: Quoted for quiet, lonely nights. 漏 is the water-clock; 漏断 means the night is far gone. The ci goes on to describe a lone wild goose.
usage.zh: 用于描写寂静孤独的夜晚。“漏”指漏壶，“漏断”即夜深。词的下文写孤鸿。

text: 东风夜放花千树，更吹落、星如雨
pinyin: dōng fēng yè fàng huā qiān shù, gèng chuī luò, xīng rú yǔ
literal: east · wind · night · releases · flowers · thousand · trees, even · blows · down, stars · like · rain
natural: the east wind at night opens flowers on a thousand trees, and blows down stars like rain

meaning.en: Opening of Xin Qiji's Lantern Festival ci: fireworks and lanterns blossom like flowers in the night wind and fall like a rain of stars.
meaning.zh: 辛弃疾元夕词的开头：东风吹开千树“花灯”，又吹落如雨的烟花星火。

equivalents: fireworks like flowers and falling stars
the Lantern Festival night in full glow

examples.zh: “东风夜放花千树，更吹落、星如雨”，写尽了元宵夜的繁华。
examples.en: 'The east wind at night opens flowers on a thousand trees, and blows down stars like rain' captures all the splendour of the Lantern Festival night.

examples.zh: 元宵晚会的烟花升空时，主持人念起了东风夜放花千树，更吹落、星如雨。
examples.en: As the fireworks rose at the Lantern Festival gala, the host recited 'the east wind at night opens flowers on a thousand trees, and blows down stars like rain'.

story.en: Xin Qiji (1140-1207), a Southern Song general-poet, wrote this ci about the Lantern Festival crowds, in which he seeks one person standing apart from the glitter.
story.zh: 南宋将领兼词人辛弃疾（1140—1207）写元夕观灯的人群，并寻觅那位独立于繁华之外的人。

usage.en: A favourite quotation at the Lantern Festival (元宵). The ci ends with '众里寻他千百度……灯火阑珊处'.
usage.zh: 元宵节常引。词的结尾为“众里寻他千百度……灯火阑珊处”。

text: 醉里挑灯看剑，梦回吹角连营
pinyin: zuì lǐ tiǎo dēng kàn jiàn, mèng huí chuī jiǎo lián yíng
literal: drunk · in · trim · lamp · look at · sword, dream · return · blow · horn · linked · camps
natural: drunk, I trim the lamp to look at my sword; waking from dreams I hear bugles sounding through the linked camps

meaning.en: Xin Qiji's longing to fight for the lost north: a drunken glance at his sword, a dream of the army camps.
meaning.zh: 辛弃疾壮志难酬的心声：醉中拨亮灯火端详宝剑，梦里回到号角连营的军旅生活。

equivalents: a warrior's dream of battle in peacetime
unfulfilled martial ambition

examples.zh: “醉里挑灯看剑，梦回吹角连营”写出了辛弃疾对沙场的向往。
examples.en: 'Drunk, I trim the lamp to look at my sword; I dream of bugles sounding through the camps' expresses Xin Qiji's yearning for the battlefield.

examples.zh: 退伍多年的老兵常说，自己仍会醉里挑灯看剑，梦回吹角连营。
examples.en: Veterans discharged for many years often say they still, in their dreams, 'trim the lamp to look at the sword and hear bugles through the camps'.

origin.source: 辛弃疾《破阵子·为陈同甫赋壮词以寄之》

story.en: Xin Qiji wrote this ci for his friend Chen Liang (Tongfu), recalling his youth as a rebel fighter against the Jin in the north.
story.zh: 辛弃疾写给友人陈亮（同甫）的壮词，追忆自己早年在北方抗金的军旅生活。

usage.en: Quoted for martial spirit and unfulfilled ambition. The poem ends '可怜白发生'.
usage.zh: 用于表达尚武精神和壮志未酬。词的结尾是“可怜白发生”。

text: 郁孤台下清江水，中间多少行人泪
pinyin: yù gū tái xià qīng jiāng shuǐ, zhōng jiān duō shǎo xíng rén lèi
literal: Yugu · Terrace · below · clear · river · water, within · how many · travellers' · tears
natural: beneath Yugu Terrace flows the clear river; how many travellers' tears are mixed in it

meaning.en: Opening of Xin Qiji's ci on a wall at Zaokou: the river carries the tears of refugees from the fall of the north.
meaning.zh: 辛弃疾题壁词的开头：郁孤台下的江水里，融着多少流亡者的泪水。

equivalents: a river fed by refugees' tears
the grief of those driven from home

examples.zh: “郁孤台下清江水，中间多少行人泪”，写的是南渡难民的悲痛。
examples.en: 'Beneath Yugu Terrace flows the clear river; how many travellers' tears are in it' is about the grief of refugees who fled south.

examples.zh: 走到赣江边，导游念起郁孤台下清江水，中间多少行人泪。
examples.en: Standing by the Gan River, the guide recited 'beneath Yugu Terrace flows the clear river; how many travellers' tears are in it'.

origin.source: 辛弃疾《菩萨蛮·书江西造口壁》

story.en: Xin Qiji wrote this ci on the wall at Zaokou (Jiangxi), where the Song empress dowager had fled from Jin troops around 1129.
story.zh: 辛弃疾题于江西造口壁上，当年（约1129年）隆祐太后曾在此逃避金兵。

usage.en: Quoted at Ganzhou's Yugu Terrace and for the grief of exile. The next line is 西北望长安，可怜无数山.
usage.zh: 在赣州郁孤台和写流亡之痛时常引用。下一句为“西北望长安，可怜无数山”。
